title.narrative: Priority River Basins Flood Risk Management Project

description.narrative: The Government of Nepal has requested the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to support the development of the Priority River Basins Flood Risk Management Project, which focuses on seven priority river basins in the Terai Region: West Rapti, Mawa-Ratuwa, Lakhandehi, Mohana, Khutiya, East Rapti, and Bakraha. Collectively, 22,000 ha of the priority river basins and 95,000 people are exposed to 1-in-50-year flood. The project areas have minimal reactive embankment interventions, which provide limited flood protection. Between 1991 and 2015, the priority river basins experienced 390 floods, of which: (i) 35 floods caused economic damage of at least NRe1 million; (ii) 37 floods caused a total of 440 deaths; and (iii) 79 floods caused total destruction of more than 10 households. The flood risk is expected to increase as more people and assets locate in vulnerable areas in the Terai Region, which will be further exacerbated by climate change. The project aims to reduce flood-related economic and social losses in the priority river basins by strengthening integrated disaster risk management approaches. The direct project beneficiaries include local communities within the project area, DWRI, and the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM). Public sector support is justified as it is unlikely that the private sector would invest as project benefits are mainly social.

10 Nov 2020 | Article: https://www.adb.org/news/features/protecting-valuable-agricultural-lands-destructive-floods-nepal
17,593 m of embankments; 17,113 m of launching aprons and 15,283 m of Revetments constructed. 255 spurs completed.

19 trainings, orientations and workshops on PRBFRMP, IFRM, Asset management System and Safeguard and OHS were given to DWRI, PRPFRMP, field offices, contractors and local government and communities. A total 277 no. of participants including 32 no. (11.6 %) of women participation.
CBDRM Consultant will further assess training needs provide training, if required. The CBDRM Consultant recruitment process is ongoing. EoI Evaluation Report is expected in August.
29 Sep 2020 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/adb-approves-50-million-assistance-address-flooding-nepal-river-basins
7,529 m of bio-engineering embankment (turfing along the embankment) completed.

Altogether 23 training programs and 4 workshops and 1 overseas observation visit have been conducted to enhance the knowledge of DWRI staff on flood protection, O&M and Asset Management. In total there were 405 participants (345 male and 60 female). Female participation 14.81%. The low percentage is due lack of women engineers in DWRI and FOs.
Annual O&M plan and budget for five FFEWS prepared and submitted to DHM for endorsement: The plan will be prepared and budget estimated, and submitted to DHM for approval and adopt in due time.
CBDRM consultant recruitment is ongoing. The EOI evaluation report is expected in November 2023. The plan will be prepared once the consultants are onboard.
FFEWS package procured and contractor has been mobilized. Equipment is procured and 80% of the equipment items are received. EA is working with contractor and consultant for installation.
Grant 0741: 65% of contracts awarded and 24% disbursed as of 14 May 2025
Loan 3977: 67% of contracts awarded and 40% disbursed as of 14 May 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: Construction of two flood control works in two river basins commenced in March 2022. Detailed engineering designs for three other river basins were completed and procurement is ongoing with contract awards targeted for December 2022. Development of flood forecasting and early warning system will be initiated in Q3 2022.

Project has prepared manuals on construction supervision; quality assurance and quality control; and asset maintenance. TRTA team has reviewed the Maintenance Manual and their suggestions/comments is being addressed. Other manuals related to river training shall be prepared whenever necessary. TRTA has prepared Asset Management System and training at the field level have been completed. DWRI has budget for the data collection for rivers within the jurisdiction of Federal government.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Feb 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/52195/52195-001-apfs-en_2.pdf
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Jun 2020: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/52195/52195-001-iee-en.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Jan 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/52195/52195-001-smr-en_4.pdf
TA 6568: 75% disbursed as of 14 May 2025
Tenders and Contracts Awarded: https://www.adb.org/projects/52195-001/main#project-tenders

The contract for the flood forecasting and early warning system (FFEWS) was signed on 2 May 2022. The contractor has mobilized, completed the site selection and field survey, and submitted the Inception Report. The contractor is involved in the programming of the software as per the site conditions. About 80% of the equipment has received. The Project Office (DHM) is verifying the equipment as per the contract Technical Speciation.

The infrastructure construction works have started. Priority has been given to women, Dalits and indigenous peoples depending on the nature of the job and their skill. Of the total labors involved, male are 80.89% and female are 19.06%; 11.90% B/C, 72.84% Janajati, 5.49% Dalit, 9.76% Madhesi and 0.01% PWD.
